utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the end of your report, you list the sources that you used or relied upon to draft this expert report; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And one of the main sources that you relied upon in your expert report were witness statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, you relied upon 21 witness statements in drafting your report.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: True, 1 through 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And these witness statements assisted you in determining the facts, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These witness statements assisted me in producing my report. The theory behind this was a fact is always empirical, so if we take a fact to mean just that, then I suppose you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also used these witness statements in arriving it at your conclusions; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And some of these witness statements are the only information you possess in relation to certain facts and conclusions.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's how they are reflected in the report, well, then, that's probably the case. One thing I should say is I also used other sources available to me and this statement was used to confirm what I was already saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies to my learned friend. I never realised, when looking at the expert report, that the witness invoked 21 different witnesses. I only saw three direct references to witness statements and some other statements that he may have been using but which he did not actually invoke in his report, or in the main body of his report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: These witness statements, sir, were given in Belgrade, Novi Sad, or to ICTY investigators; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you use any of the transcripts or any of the testimony from this particular trial in producing this report?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The transcript was available to me since the Defence were submitting to me whichever documents they had in their possession. I had the transcript of the testimony of that gentleman who was an operative at the command of the Guards Brigade as well as the testimony of Mr. Vojinovic, the commander of the 80th Brigade, at least as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So those are the only two transcripts that you used in drafting this report?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, or as least I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you were also present, I believe, for the testimony of Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you present for the testimony of Mr. Pringle?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I left when Mr. Theunens's testimony finished. The only thing I had from Mr. Pringle was the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, are you aware that these 21 witness statements have not been introduced as evidence in this court? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say I'm really that aware of it. However, I do know that witness statements are not certified as authentic unless the relevant witness eventually appears, if I may put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let us move on. In your report, at page 109 in the English, which is paragraph 20 - I think it's about page 101/102 in the B/C/S - do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In your report, in conclusion number 20, you indicate that "the 3rd Assault Group was stronger than a reinforced company and the reinforcements were of a higher command level than the company itself." And in parentheses you put "TO detachments." Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that the Petrova Gora TO, the Leva Supoderica TO, and certain members of the Vukovar TO were part of Captain Radic's 3rd Assault Group?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, have you followed or did you follow the hearings in Belgrade in relation to the Ovcara incident? Because I know you cited a number of transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't follow, but I did have the relevant transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware that Miroljub Vujevic has given a statement or has testified in Belgrade that he was under Captain Radic's command? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR FORCA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to refer my colleague back to the transcript of the 23rd of June, 2006; 11.134 that's the page, and the line reference is 12. The Defence was trying to use statements that the witness had not used in his report, and the Presiding Judge said, "What is not important is for you to try to show the witness that there is evidence contrary to what he has invoked." And the Defence is told that all these contradictory statements will be evaluated in due course and that I had no right to ask questions of that nature. Therefore, Your Honours, I believe my learned friend should be aware of that, and the only thing he can ask questions about are things that we used in the report. I think this was a very important ruling for our Defence and I think the same ruling should then mutatis mutandis to the OTP as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, we're dealing with an expert witness. It's one thing to learn from him the source of any factual basis for his expert report and the conclusions he's reached. But he's not a witness to the facts; he is an independent expert who really has simply accepted from various sources that certain things are the fact. Now, those things will either be established by evidence before us or will not. It's with a witness as to facts, the cross-examination may, and often has in this Court both for Defence and Prosecution, put to the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: other people, X, Y, Z or whatever, have said it differently? That's because the witness is speaking of his knowledge and recollection to the facts and you are then testing how strong how his satisfaction personally is about those facts or whether he is aware that there are competing views. But this witness is not in that category. He's not speaking of facts as of his own knowledge; he's merely saying: In my report, I have accepted this to be true, that to be true, that to be true. And you rightly have been exploring some of the sources of those, but it's nothing to do with his credit that some other witnesses may have a different view of the facts. Do you see the distinction between an expert witness and a witness as to the facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I see that, Your Honour, but may I ask him about testimony that the defendant, who he's here on behalf of, has made certain statements which are in conflict with his report? May I confront him with those?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may, but you will -- and that is because it's directly evidence of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, as the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that might have shortened something that you were going to do, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would agree, Your Honour. And having a bit of the flu, the quicker I'm out of here, the safer everyone here is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, Captain Radic testified last week that the Territorial Defence and the Leva Supoderica units which were along his axis were part of his assault group. He testified to that on pages 12.617 to 12.618. Are you aware of this testimony?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: What you can find in my report was written before Mr. Radic took the stand. As for the facts at which you seem to have arrived, this may be something that a number of different witnesses spoke about, but it is definitely not something that I knew of when I wrote my report. On the other hand, if you look at my report, specifically page 96, paragraph 127 - that's the Serbian reference - I said how the functioning of the command system in the Guards Brigade worked, above all, in the Motorised Battalion or, if you like, Assault Detachment 1. And that is in relation to the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion, or JOD 1. If you look at that portion of my report, I think the following may be deduced: The second bullet or dash, if you look at that, I quote: "Vukovar TO units were organised and initially they coordinated with the combat operations of his battalion and JOD until the second half of October, and afterwards, by the 18th of November, 1991, at the latest, they were under his immediate command."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, that whole paragraph, 127 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That whole paragraph, 127, that comes from the testimony of Major Tesic before the war crimes chamber in Belgrade; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes. Not only before the war crimes chamber in Belgrade but also the statements that he provided to the Hague investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is there an objection, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I want you to finish and the witness to finish. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I've been following what my learned friend has been saying. I found no reference in the transcript to Miroslav Radic saying "my assault group" or "the Leva Supoderica detachment." He did speak about the assault group comprising Vujanovic and Leva Supoderica. But he never said that the 3rd Company was part of that assault group. I followed closely. I didn't mean to interrupt, but this is simply not something that Miroslav Radic stated. He said who was in command of the 3rd Assault Group. The fact that the witness interpreted the note in his own way is one thing and what Radic said is another, and they are not the same thing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us that paragraph 127 is based on statements of Major Tesic. I've indicated to you that, in this court, there has been testimony from Captain Radic that the assault group "consisted of members of the Territorial Defence along my axis and of members of the Leva Supoderica detachment." Now that you're aware of Captain Radic's testimony before this court, would you now accept that those groups were part of Captain Radic's 3rd Assault Group?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, sir, within your report, you've indicated that Kameni Lancuzanin and Miroljub Vujevic received their orders from Tesic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: That is correct. I only indicated what had been previously stated by the commander of the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're relying on Major Tesic's statements when you say "commander of the 1st Battalion" to arrive at that decision or arrive at that conclusion; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, within your report, you've relied upon the statement of Major Tesic, both from his statements to the OTP -- I'm sorry, the Prosecutor's office, as well as his statements to the court in Belgrade, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, would you agree that you cited his statements 12 times in your report, or you footnoted them 12 times in your report? Or several times, if it's ...

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes, several times. I did footnote that several times in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And on page 71, you footnoted -- in the English, you footnoted his report to the ICTY; isn't that correct? That should be about page 64 in the B/C/S. Paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Is that about footnote 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In that case, the answer is yes, I did refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have that report with you, sir, that statement?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 15 of that statement which you've referred to, which is on page 5, Mr. Tesic says the following: "Around mid-October 1991, on orders from OG South, the two Guards Motorised Brigade battalions changed their names to assault detachments, JOD, and their guards companies became assault groups. With this change, the TO of Vukovar was integrated into the assault companies, i.e., TO Vukovar was subordinated to the JNA at a much lower level than before. The TO detachment within the 1st Assault Group was led by Stanko Vujanovic - Taksista. The 3rd Assault Group, commanded by Milorad Radic, also comprised a TO Vukovar detachment led by Miroljub Vujevic which comprised the TO Petrova Gora as well as the Leva Supoderica detachments, numbering between 30 and 40 men, whose commander was Milan Lancuzanin - Kameni. This last group called themselves Seseljevski, or Seselj's men." Were you aware of that statement within the interview?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Sir, Your Honours, I can distinguish at least three questions there. The first is about footnote 5. Footnote 5 only tells you what the tasks or objectives were in Vukovar, which is something that Tesic said, commander of the Motorised Battalion. Secondly, in order to understand the phenomenon or the process that was Operation Vukovar - and I think the gentleman's question can be viewed in that context - and in connection with what we said yesterday about the command and control system from brigade level down to squad level, and further, in connection with the statements that I used, I think the following is what matters: Firstly, a written order or a decision by the commander of OG South, or rather, first and foremost, the Guards Brigade and later OG South, those that are available to the Chamber as Exhibits 405, 408, 410, 430 and 431, these were supplemented in keeping with the working method applied in all joint and operative units. These were supplemented verbally. You can see that if you look at the war log produced by the Guards Brigade, or OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but that's not the question I asked you. The question I asked you was: Were you aware of that statement within this interview? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Sir, in my conclusion or rather, in drawing my conclusions, I used the methods enumerated in the introduction; that is to say, if the commander of the 1st Battalion, or JOD 1, says, "I was in direct command, they were under my command," then I take it at face value. "Company commanders and commanders of TO came to get their assignments from me," sir, this is what I used in drawing my conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, once again, I will ask you the same question: Were you aware of this statement in the interview; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I can't give you a specific answer because I used the elements that I mentioned to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In this statement, Major Tesic has stated: "The 3rd Assault Group, commanded by Milorad Radic, also comprised a TO Vukovar detachment, led by Miroljub Vujevic, which comprised the TO Petrova Gora as well as the Leva Supoderica detachments." Will you take it at face value, using your phrase, that those units were part of Captain Radic's 3rd assault company -- I'm sorry, 3rd Assault Group?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, if we continue, one more paragraph, a very short paragraph in that same statement, paragraph 19, where Major Tesic says: "I would be lying if I said that the relationship between Captain Miroslav Radic and Kameni or Vujevic was not friendly. I know that Radic's orders were fully complied with." First question, if you could just tell us yes or no: Do you recall that statement in the interview which you've cited in your report?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, is that not an indication Radic gave them orders and tasks and that they complied with those orders and tasks?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree that Major Tesic was in a far better position than you to indicate who the persons were within Radic's 3rd Assault Group?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we've had testimony from Captain Radic that he would draw up the plans for combat actions and issue the tasks based on those plans to the assault group commanders. And that's at page 12.621. Sir, isn't that consistent with the view that Captain Radic wrote the plans, gave the orders, gave the tasks to those TO brigade -- TO unit commanders?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, once again, I have to go back to my evidence given yesterday concerning the work process from the brigade command level down to the squad commander, that is to say, two levels above and two levels below the company commander. Plans, as documents, are not binding at the level of the company. This is one part of my answer. The second part is they had -- or he had the command of Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora on his own terms. The commander of JOD 1 or the Motorised Battalion was in command. We can now analyse various documents, orders, decisions, in order to look into the entire process. This is what I started out with and then the learned gentleman interrupted me. And only if we did that would we be able to make our conclusions based on the entirety of this material. So, to conclude, a plan is not a document which is produced at the level of a company, and in his statement, in the stated detachments, this is what it says. And if one looks at the first order of commander of brigade and various other ones, it emerges that the commander of the battalion, or JOD 1, was in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that Captain Radic was solely responsible for planning combat operations of that assault group; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, planning and activities of the 1st Motorised Battalion, or JOD 1, were in the jurisdiction of the command of JOD 1. In that sense, all commanders who were subordinated to the commander of JOD 1 received their tasks. In accordance with these tasks, that is to say, on the basis of what was planned at the level of the command of JOD 1, company commanders, as basic units or assault groups, carried out orders.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In the previous answer, it should be "plans as documents are not mandatory at the level of the company not "not binding at the level of the company."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, again, Mr. Radic testified last week and I want to put this to you. He stated: "If one wants to control and plan --" I'm sorry, that's at page 12.620, beginning lines 14: "If one wants to control and plan any combat activity, be it an attack or a defence, excuse me, one needs to do that thoroughly because the outcome of that operation depends on it. Since I mentioned a moment ago that I was the only officer who had completed the military academy, I didn't want to leave it to chance that anyone should plan combat operations except for myself." Having heard Captain Radic's testimony that he didn't want to leave it for anyone to plan combat operations except for himself, will you accept that he was the person who planned combat operations for that assault group?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I apologise, would you please specify which assault group? Do you mean the detachments?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The 3rd Assault Group, sir.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, once again, I must say that my report was compiled prior to Captain Radic giving evidence here. Based on what the gentleman just stated, I would partially agree with it and I would partially agree with it. This pertains to the evidence given by Mr. Radic. In principle, the commander is responsible for his unit, and it is true that in the 3rd Company, only Captain Radic was a graduate of the military academy. On the other hand, given that I used the statement saying that, since they were along the same axis and since they were in the same sector, the same task was given to the company commanders and said detachments, that cannot be considered as evidence of Captain Radic being competent to plan their activities. Or, as we established yesterday, the person who issues the decision, who issues the order, is the one in command. He also supervises the execution of the orders. Given that the said detachments were in the axis or in the sector of JOD 1, then I, as an expert, could only agree that, possibly in compliance with the decision of the commander of JOD 1, Captain Radic was able to assist, given that he was a highly trained officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant to raise this in redirect, but the context will be lost by then. I read what was put to the witness about the statement of Captain Radic, but it would have been fair if it had been explained to the witness that this pertained to the system of communications, because that is the context. No planning of main operations or tasks is mentioned in that context. No. Only the system of communications was mentioned, because he wanted to protect it for security reasons, and he spoke of codes, encryption, and so on. I don't need to read the entire statement to you now. I apologise. My colleague is suggesting something to me. And then he says that he conveyed the system of communication to his platoons, even along the same axis. He conveyed it to the TO detachment. And the question put to the witness had a completely different meaning. So, in order for me not to continuously jump to my feet and interrupt the process, perhaps the entire context could, in the future, be explained to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, you were there doing what you are concerned that Mr. Weiner is doing. You are putting on the words your interpretation of their meaning and the context in which they should be understood. You complain Mr. Weiner is doing that. You differ as to what they should each be. Now, Mr. Weiner is entitled to put the words that were used to the witness. Whether that will affect his opinion in his report is one thing. Just what the effect of the evidence of your client may be on some of the factual assumptions in this report is an entirely different thing again and one which this Chamber will have to determine. So I'd suggest that interventions of that nature are really best left to re-examination, when the time comes. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, I just want to place it in context. If you look at lines 3 through 6 of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's no need to debate that. That's really final address stuff, unless you want to change the sense of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not at all. I'm just saying that it wasn't taken out of context.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that in relation to the orders that came from the battalion or the brigade as the times to go into action, to coordinate with the rest of the other units, Captain Radic was the person who received those orders and he, in turn, would issue the combat plans or action plans; as well as the orders from the battalion and the brigade, which he received, he would then issue those to the commanders of the assault group. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No, but I have to explain, or rather, it could be both no and yes. First of all, I have no information that Captain Radic received any kind of orders from the brigade command directly. That means that I have no such information. Second, the plans of combat operations, the plan as a document, is not something that is drafted at the level of a company. Third, orders for operations, as you termed it, or rather, in the course of operations, were given both to Captain Radic and to commanders of the said detachments. If that's what he said, if that's what the commander said, then I believe it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Then that's fine."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll read it to you. On page 12.621, beginning at line 6: "Since I used to draw up such plans before any action, for reasons of security, I would do that immediately prior, prior to action. I never drew up a plan and set it aside for the next two days or so but I always do it the night before. Since we coordinated, and since the battalion commander would tell us the exact time when we were to go into action at the level of battalion and the brigade, I always issued those orders to those commanders which were part of the assault group immediately prior to going into action, that is the morning ..." Based on that, sir, would you agree that Captain Radic was receiving the orders from the battalion level and he was the one who was issuing them to the assault battalion -- I'm sorry, to the assault group commanders? And he would also issue his plans or tasks to them so they could go into combat action.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, if what Captain Radic referred to as "plan" entailed sketches and drawings of the area, of the terrain, given that this is a settlement and they needed, for example, to take a building or a house, then I understand what he said. And in reply to your two questions, first, you, yourself, said that he only conveyed the particular moment when one needed to go into action. He did not convey his own plan, as you said, not to the other units to which he was not the commander. So these other units, the particular detachments had their orders, and in the text that you read out, it says that Captain Radic only conveyed the particular time when they were to go into action. He didn't convey to everyone his plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're basing your conclusion on the statements of Major Tesic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: That he issued orders to company commanders and detachment commanders, yes. As for the statement that you read out about the moment the -- the moment of time they were supposed to go into action, based on what you read out ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So I take that as a yes. You're basing your opinion on the statements made by Mr. Tesic; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Those statements including.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's continue on. You utilised what you referred to as a handwritten diary of the 1st Motorised Battalion command?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that that handwritten document is not the official or actual diary but it's only the selected entries; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you have a copy of that with you? Or I could show it on the screen if you don't.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I haven't got a copy with me, except for what is included in the charts in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we please see Exhibit 807, please. Could see the final two pages, pages 10 and 11 which concern November 10th onward, which would be 0010 and 11 in the B/C/S. 2714-0010.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree that -- first, do you have it in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that from November 10th onwards, the words "resubordination, attachment, detachment," are not used anywhere in that diary in relation to the Petrova Gora or Leva Supoderica TO units? Could you look closely at those two pages?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: All I can see is the 10th, 11th and 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you be shown the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: That's true. I have not found such words as "attachment" or "resubordination."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And would you also agree with me that nowhere in those last two days are the words stated: "Captain Radic no longer commands the 3rd Assault Group"?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes. That's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that those assault groups remained active between November 17th and 21st, 1991; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to look again or refer you again to Major Tesic's report which you cite within your -- Major Tesic's interview which you cite in your report. On page 9 of that, paragraph 38, he states the following: "On 19 November, there were members of the local Serbian Vukovar TO in the hospital compound. I arrived at the hospital with a small number of men of the 1st Assault Group led by Sasa Bojkovski. Parts of the 3rd Assault Group of Captain Miroslav Radic came from the flank, from the direction of the bus station." Do you recall reading that portion of the statement when you used it in your report?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can't say I remember it verbatim but, generally speaking, I do recollect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Since Major Tesic has indicated that the 1st and 3rd Assault Groups arrived at the Vukovar Hospital on November 19th, will you agree that those assault groups were still active on at least November 19th, 1991?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But would you agree that Major Tesic was in a far better position than yourself to know the composition of the troops under his command?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move to just a very, very brief subject. Could you look at your report; page 74 in the B/C/S and 81 in the English. There's a chart or a table. Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The final part of the chart -- the final line of the chart says: "Decision by OG South commander," and it says -- and that was a decision in writing, and it says, "19 November, 1991, resubordination of the units and evacuation from the hospital." Is that a mistake? Is that just a typographical error? Would you agree that's a typographical error, that it should read the 21st of November?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No. If I may elaborate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I assume you mean the resubordination of the TO. In the commander's decision dated the 19th of November, there is mention of other units being resubordinated. And I think it was in item 2 - I'm not certain, but it must be somewhere - where there's talk of the hospital evacuation, if I remember correctly. And I don't think I would have included that in my report had I not been able to remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that there was no resubordination order issued by Colonel Mrksic on November 19th but rather the order was issued in writing on November 21st, 1991?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: The decision on the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital is dated the 19th of November, the 19th, the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm strictly speaking in terms of the second -- the first part of it. The resubordination of units, that was on the 21st, sir; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Just tell me which units, which specific units on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The Leva Supoderica and the Vukovar TO units.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Well, dear sir, what I'm telling you is, as of the 19th, there's no mention of the Leva Supoderica detachment or the TO, at least as far as I indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, no, the issue is, in this chart that you drew, you have two items occurring, two actions occurring, on 19 November 1991, and the method of communication you list is writing: "resubordination of units and evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital." Now, let's set the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital aside and just deal with resubordination of units. There was no writing in relation to the resubordination of the Leva Supoderica and the Vukovar TO units on November 19th; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the resubordination did not occur until November 21st. The order did not occur -- the order was not written until November 21st, which is Exhibit 422, which you cite in your report. You cite it at the end as a source.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: A written document on the resubordination of those units, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you aware that the resubordination was not completed until -- of those units was not completed until November 22nd, 1991?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Dear sir, although I've gone through a lot of different documents, orders, statements, I did not really focus on the period after the 19th specifically. I do know that there are reports. The reports are mentioned in the documents that I used. There is a report about how activities were being carried out throughout the post-conflict period, as I described it. I can hardly be accurate about this. I can hardly say yes to your question. "Yes, there is a report, and yes, it is possible to refer to that report," I can hardly say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you're not contesting Colonel Mrksic's order, Exhibit 425, which indicates that the resubordination was completed on November 22nd, 1991?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it must be a slip of the tongue on your part. I don't believe this could possibly have been an order. A report of a superior commander, at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit 425, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see under "Operation Group JUG Units," number 2? Do you see the fourth paragraph, "In the course of 22 November 1991..."? "In the course of 22 November 1991, according to your strictly confidential order, number 115-151, from 20 November 1991, all issues regarding release and subordination of the volunteer units have been realised."

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Can we please show the upper half, because I suppose what you are reading must be in the upper half of the document. But if you could just scroll back down for a minute, please. Up. A little further up, please. And now scroll down, if you can, please. Yes, I've read this again. I'm telling you this is not an order, this is a report. It was only a remark that I made. Because that's what it says in the heading, a regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it's signed by Colonel Mile Mrksic, commander of OG South, isn't that correct, or OG JUG?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: That is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're not contesting the validity of his statement that the resubordination was not completed until November 22nd, 1991?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I cannot cast any doubt, nor am I entitled to cast any doubt, on anything signed by the commander of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to just a very short matter that you mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, perhaps this would be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It would be a wonderful time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will break now, and the next session, I'd expect to finish no later than 20 past 12.00, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll finish much sooner than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to give you the outer limits, okay? We will resume at 10 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified that any form of political activity or politics was strictly forbidden in the command staff's units or military institutions; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I do. If necessary, I can go back to that exact portion and tell you what exactly it says. It's about any form of party affiliation in the armed forces, first and foremost. And if you want me to read the relevant portion out, I'll be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's not necessary. Unless the Court wants to hear that. No, that's not necessary. I just want to ask you: Are you aware of the background of the Leva Supoderica unit which you mention in your report and you've testified about?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I was familiar with this information to the extent that I came across such information in the documents that I indicated I had used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that it had been sponsored by the Serbian Radical Party, or Seselj's party?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure whether it was really that, whether they had been sponsored by the Serbian Radical Party. But there is information to indicate that members of the Leva Supoderica unit were close to the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're not familiar with the level of training that those particular soldiers had or received?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand what level of training we are talking about, how well-trained they were or who they were trained by. If you could try to be slightly more specific in terms of what you mean by "level of training."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's exactly what my question was. These were a group of volunteers which, in your words, were close to the Serbian Radical Party. And when I say "level of training," do you know who they were trained by or what training, if any, they had received?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was, after all, a helpful idea to ask this additional question. What were the members of the Leva Supoderica unit like? I arrived at a conclusion, or rather, I quoted a statement by the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment. This is at page 96, paragraph 127, of my report, which reads: "For a commander," this is the JOD commander talking, and I quote: "Lancuzanin, Kameni, commander of the Leva Supoderica TO worked well, did good work. He caught 30 or so members of his detachment while stealing, sent them back to Sid and removed them from the area of combat operations." Therefore, as to who trained them or how, this is not really something that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that, we've had testimony of a visit of Seselj to Vukovar. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I did come across this information in the various documents that I received from the Defence. I did come across information to indicate that Seselj was in the area of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And there has been testimony that in one of his visits, he addressed some soldiers and officers and made a statement that "no Ustasha should be allowed to leave Vukovar alive." Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, as an expert in command and control, you realise that there's a danger making a statement like that in front of non-professional soldiers, such as volunteers. Would you agree, sir?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: If a statement was made, then I would agree that this was an unprofessional thing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us what acts should a commander take when a statement like that is made in front of his troops? What acts, if any, should a commander take to make sure that there is no danger as a result of a statement of that kind?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is speculative. I do not know for a fact that such a statement was made; however, in principle - again, this is a mere assumption and as such very difficult to prove - if such a statement was made and the unit commander knows that all form of party affiliation was strictly forbidden, it would have been the natural thing to do to warn the person making such statements and also to inform his superior command. But this is a mere assumption. I do not know for a fact that this was, indeed, stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Just briefly, I think this group of questions is not related to the expert's evidence. I believe all we can derive from this line of questioning is a series of hypothetical, speculative answers, and I don't think that will do the Chamber or us any good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There may be quite a bit of truth in some of that, Mr. Weiner. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would like to continue with some hypothetical questions. I want you to assume, sir, that a company commander is told by one of his subordinates that crimes have just occurred, prisoners were beaten by some of his subordinates, and that one or more of his subordinates were involved in murders of prisoners. What action must that company commander take?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: At a purely hypothetical level, I think this hardly calls for any comment. Back in 1988, regulations were passed on the application of the international laws of war in the armed forces. Therefore, the provisions contain specific regulations in relation to the subject matter that you have just raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us what a Yugoslav or JNA officer should do in that situation?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: The JNA officer - again, this is hypothetical but in keeping with the rules - he would have to inform the relevant bodies about anything like that occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what relevant bodies must he notify?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was not a member of the security organ, but there are rules and there are tasks that are peculiar to security organs. One of the principal tasks is counter-intelligence. As far as I know, another among those tasks is possible involvement in investigating such acts as you have described.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, what if the officer fails to take these actions?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Once again, hypothetically speaking, all I can tell you is that an officer must make these steps; or, once again, hypothetically speaking, if it later transpires that he did not take those steps, then his superior will take action against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's continue. Let's assume the following: That a company commander hears that certain soldiers under his command are trying to seize prisoners, remove prisoners from a facility, and even sends a few soldiers to see what's happening. Assuming these facts, that a company commander hears that there is a serious criminal problem, what action is he required to take to prevent that from happening?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I think I've answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please answer it again?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Again, once again, in hypothetical terms, if a commander hears, if I understood you well, that a crime is being committed, a crime of that sort, then a commander will take action to prevent the consequences of it, if the crime is being committed at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What are some of the actions that he can take? Can he request military police?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: It is to be assumed that that's a possibility, too, but not directly. He must address his superior who is competent to order that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can the company commander go to the scene where the crime is occurring himself?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes, if the person taking measures to prevent whatever is taking place allows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if he is at the scene and sees his soldiers there, can he order them out of the area?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes. If he believes it necessary, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weiner. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Forca, when we were conducting the proofing of your testimony, did I inform you that, after your report was filed here, Miroslav Radic gave testimony here before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did I inform you of statements given by company commanders, Zoran Zirojevic, Davor Vuckovic, and Deputy Commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion, Slavko Stijakovic, rather, their evidence?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did we cover together parts of the transcript of their testimonies during the proofing?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you know what they testified about.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In your report submitted to the Court, is it true that you quoted only three statements?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were those statements of Tesic, Panic, and Witness P 014?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. Every one of these questions has been leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can agree, but this is beyond dispute. I took this from the screen, these three quotations. It won't make or break the issue, but I'm just drawing the attention of the Trial Chamber to this issue. But I will stop with it here. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question is: From the 10th of November --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you answer this question, could we see Exhibit 807, dated the 10th of November, 1991. Could that be put on our screens. This is a note of the 1st Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This is an entry in the war log. Do you have it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I don't have the 10th. I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. After the 10th and 11th -- rather, after the 10th of November, who was in command of the Petrova Gora TO detachment and who was the commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment, and under whose control were they after the 10th of November, 1991, following the fall of Milovo Brdo that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: After the 10th of November, there followed a decision of the commander of OG South. That was on the 14th of November. The decision was sent to detachment commanders and to their subordinate commanders. And from the 14th onwards, they could have been either under the control of the commander of OG South, because that was the decision taken by the commander of OG South, to split JOD 1 and the 1st Motorised Battalion. So they could have been either under his command or under the command of the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion, given that, in the first order dated the 1st of October, 1991, an order issued by the commander of the Guards Brigade, it was precisely him who was appointed commander of JOD 1. And he said himself: "They were under my command, under my control, up until the 18th of November."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At any point in time - I'm deliberately referring to these dates from the 10th of November to the 18th of November - the Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica detachments, were they under -- at any time, under the command or any sort of control of Miroslav Radic?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: In my view, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today, my learned friend asked you about statements that you quoted. My question is: You mentioned quoting documents as well.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you use the war log and the operations log? Rather, I'm interested in -- not in hearing whether you quoted them but whether you used them.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes. I was waiting for the transcript to complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you also consult decisions and orders, combat reports, and everything else comprising military documentation?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If a statement is consistent with military documentation and other documents used by you, did you also quote a part of that statement -- part of that witness statement?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. And if a witness statement is not corroborated by military or other documentation, did you quote such a statement in your report?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that the statements of Major Tesic put to you by my learned friend were not quoted by you precisely for those reasons? Because they were not corroborated --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object. This is a cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a cross-examination, not a redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are certainly, Mr. Borovic, going beyond what is proper in form for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] All right. Let's leave it for the Trial Chamber to rule on this ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please answer this: My learned friend read out to you a statement on page 12.620, line 14. I'm going to read to you 12.620, line 21, where Captain Radic says: "In order to protect data and communication systems, I was the sole person doing that. That means that every night, following the completion of daily activities, I would go to a separate room and draw a system of communications for each squad commander, using codes of different colours and geographical terms, and so on." Does this pertain to tasks and plans, what I just read out, as my learned friend asked you; or does this pertain exclusively to the system of communication between Radic and his platoon and squad commanders?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: It pertains, first and foremost, to communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. To my learned friend's question, you said as follows: "Captain Radic received tasks, as did commanders of Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica TO detachments. If this is what the commander said, then yes, I do believe it." Which commander did you have in mind? Because it wasn't clear from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I meant the commander of JOD 1, that is to say, the 1st Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You used footnotes where you quoted statements by Tesic. Since my learned friends have this, I would like to turn now to footnote 54. I read all of these footnotes to the deputy commander of the battalion, and he replied to footnotes 54, 56, 66, 68, 86 and 90. When it comes to positions given in these footnotes in your report, do you still stand by them?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. This is a reference that the Chamber will verify, and, as I said, I covered all of these footnotes with the deputy of Major Tesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer have the war log on our screens - could we please put it back - the entries made by Slavko Stijakovic, and this is Exhibit 807, dated the 10th of -- it won't take me long, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Globally speaking - and you had this when you were drawing your report - does it say anywhere, from the 10th of November onwards, do you see in this war log of the 1st Motorised Battalion that Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica detachments are mentioned anywhere? Are they mentioned anywhere between the 10th and 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you now please turn to the 10th of November. Does it say there: "Based on the previous plan of attack, the battalion conducted an operation and captured Milovo Brdo, the last important feature in the axis of attack of the battalion"? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Based on the topic of your report, is this consistent with your report?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. That's outside of the cross-examination. He's repeating examination-in-chief at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I don't recall any cross-examination on this point. Have I forgotten it, Mr. Borovic, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to remind my learned friend that he cross-examined the witness precisely about the events from the 10th to the 18th. It was definitely covered in cross-examination. I noted it down. That's why I wanted to check with the witness which parts he used for his report. If you believe that this is irrelevant for redirect, then I can withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment, I've not yet caught up with the connection. It may be there, but I don't see it. Either you explain it more or move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the witness was examined about JOD 1 and whether members of the 1st Motorised Battalion were within the composition of JOD 1, and when this expert was examined, it was suggested then -- it was suggested to the witness that members of the Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica detachments, during this period of time referred to in the log, were together with the 3rd Motorised Company of Captain Radic. This is precisely why I asked whether they were mentioned anywhere and whether, between the 10th and 18th, they are recorded as being on the same axis, and whether Captain Radic and his company was, throughout that whole time, in the sector of Milovo Brdo or whether he was someplace else defined as the axis of operation of JOD 1. We can go and check the entries from the 10th to the 18th and then ask whether it says anywhere else that the 3rd Company of Miroslav Radic moved anywhere else from the sector of Milovo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have concluded this particular topic, Your Honours. Thank you. Thank you for your understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Radic gave evidence before this Chamber. He explained many things and I will now turn to only part of his evidence concerning the order of Borivoje Tesic, for which he says he received it on the 19th of November via a Motorola. Miroslav Radic also stated that -- I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Again, that was not raised on cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought you put very specifically that the only written order was two days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, no. Now they're into going to the hospital pursuant to an order via Motorola, an oral order by Borislav [sic] Tesic on the 19th to go to the hospital. That's outside of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I agree a Motorola has been mentioned, but at the moment there's no identification of the order being the hospital order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Except from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As soon as we hear "19th of November via Motorola," that's what they've been arguing through witness after witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Borovic, are we talking to the order to go to the hospital or the order for resubordination, both of which were noted by this witness as being on the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was going to leave it for the end, about the hospital and resubordination. What I wanted to turn to now is the order that Miroslav Radic received via a Motorola from Major Borivoje Tesic. He said that and the Prosecutor claimed that he had not received that order but rather than Captain Sasa Bojkovski received a verbal order. This is why I want to put to the expert witness something he didn't have before; namely, the testimony of the accused about which he was cross-examined by the Prosecution claiming that he did not receive an order from Major Tesic but rather that Bojkovski received. And this has to do with the order of Tesic as to who was securing the hospital from the outside, and that's quite important.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to say, I haven't raised that with this witness; I've raised it with others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I do not, at the moment, Mr. Borovic, recall this point being raised in cross-examination by Mr. Weiner of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the part that was shown the witness by my learned friend to the effect that, outside the hospital, on the 19th of November, he was with Bojkovski on behalf of the 1st Assault Group securing the hospital, and that Radic came from the other side of the hospital. That's what I'm trying to say, what Radic said in relation to that. Page 20 and page 37, my colleagues are telling me. Because that's contrary to what Tesic is saying, exactly the opposite. But if you think I'm now evaluating evidence, no problem. I suppose, I'm sure ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm going to be with you this time, Mr. Borovic, because you've reminded me enough of one passage of cross-examination, so go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So, if this is what Radic stated, if he said that they were always on the same channel of these Motorolas, the question is: What about the other company commanders? If the Motorolas were on the same channel all the time, would they not have been able to hear Major Borivoje Tesic's order for Captain Radic to go and secure the hospital on the 19th of November?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Certainly, yes, as long as the channel was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And now more for what my learned friend from the OTP really want to know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have paragraph 63 of Tesic's statement? Because that's the one that I'm invoking. Can the OTP please track that down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 63 reads as follows, and this is Tesic's statement, a statement given by Borivoje Tesic to the OTP: "What I remember as being on the 19th or the 20th of November, 1991 (I can't remember the exact date) are the daily briefings in the evening in relation to the combat operations. At the command post of OG South, in Negoslavci, at about 1800 hours, the commander of OG South, Colonel Mile Mrksic, issued a verbal order to resubordinate the Vukovar TO. Mrksic's verbal order was to the effect that the Vukovar TO would now cease to be subordinate to the Guards Brigade but would continue to be subordinate to the 80th Motorised Brigade, as well as the fact that the order would take effect immediately. That same evening, been 8.00 and 9.00, I informed my own company commanders and conveyed this order to them." Mr. Forca, have you heard what I just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment on that?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Your Honours, the process of the work of commands is something that we commented upon sufficiently yesterday. I will just briefly repeat what I said yesterday. Whenever there's a written order, a written command or any other sort of order, it must be preceded by a decision. The way this statement has now been read back to me, the statement made by the commander of the 1st Battalion, the portion read back to me by Mr. Borovic, this means that the commander of OG South decided, and later confirmed this in writing, that what was indicated there would be carried out, that is, the resubordination of the TO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Additionally, you said under the command and control of the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment, until the 18th of November - that's what you said - when the need ceased for JOD 1 to continue to exist. There were only the Petrova Gora TO detachment and the Leva Supoderica TO detachment left. If Mrksic gave a verbal order to Major Tesic saying now that he nothing more to do with the Vukovar TO, would that not mean that he, too, after the 18th, ceased to have any sort of control over the Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora TO detachments?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's a speech, as well as leading, and it's also outside of the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I won't enter into the last part, but there is a lot of leading and it is rather a discursive way of approaching a question, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Between the 18th and the evening of the 19th or possibly the 20th - unless the witness cannot remember exactly - who has control over the Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora TO detachments?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: If there was a verbal communication by the OG commander to the effect that the above-mentioned TO detachments were not under the command of the commander of the 1st Battalion, it would have been possible for them to be under his command; or they were somewhere on the ground, under the command of their own commanders, the commanders of those detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which commanders do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: I mean Lancuzanin and Vujevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If, at the point, the commander of the Vukovar TO existed at all, would he not have been in command of those two detachments?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Indeed, he would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Just to wrap this up. My learned friend was asking you questions about some matters that were of a rather legal nature. I won't be going that far. There is no doubt that a crime occurred in the Ovcara area. In your opinion, if this was indeed his area of responsibility, do you think the commander of the 80th Motorised Brigade would have been responsible in any way at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is he asking for legal responsibility? Criminal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, if there is a deficiency there, is that not in the questions that you put?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I asked for the role of a commander. If he wants to ask for a role of a commander in that position ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I hadn't understood this in any other sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I hope the witness understands it in that sense, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the witness well understands. Thank you, Mr. Weiner. Carry on, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You were talking about the town command. If, in an area where the town commander exists, and in this case it's Ovcara, would it not be the town commander being the one bearing responsibility for any crime occurring?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about in the units subordinate to the town commander? Under the assumption that they happen to be in the area when a crime was in the offing, so to speak, there were prisoners being mistreated and, according to some, even killed, would the town commander not have been duty-bound to put a stop to any activity? Would he not have been duty-bound to inform someone, a military authority?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: Yes, insofar as he had the power to put a stop to anything like that going on, he would have been duty-bound. If he did see all these things going on, he was required to stop it. If, indeed, he was unable to stop it, then he should have asked his superior for someone to stop it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What if the commander of the 80th Motorised Brigade said, "I found about the crime at Ovcara only the following day"? Would he still have been required to inform someone to report this crime or take any steps at all?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: We've gone through that. According to the regulations, and we've read them back several times, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: While you were working on your report, did you come across any document at all about the military disciplinary or legal responsibility, or steps, disciplinary steps, being taken about anyone from the 80th Kraljevic Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Will you understand the facts to be this?  Are you aware that
utterances.text: No. I never came across anything to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Forca, thank you very much for your answers. Your Honours, this concludes my re-examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't sure if I should wait for the witness to leave, since we have two brief matters to raise. The first one is the OTP motion and the other thing is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May we thank you, Professor, for the evidence that you've given, your report, and for your preparedness to come here and assist in this trial. You will be pleased to know that you may now return to your other occupation. And we would like to thank you for taking the trouble to be with us. The court officer will show you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. My appearance might become tiresome for you, since I'm springing to my feet all the time these days. It is for that reason that I have the following proposal to make: I think it should be Ms. Tapuskovic who will be informing about all these things and who will be tendering 92 bis statements by two witnesses. This is the last I have to say today, and again, I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Ms. Tapuskovic.
